title.narrative: Joint Programme on Local Governance, JPLG I

description.narrative: At the level of the programmes overall objective (Local governance contributes to peace and equitable service delivery) the indicators relate to three intended outcomes: • Access to basic services improved; • Political and social stability enhanced For objective one (Communities have equitable access to basic services through local government) four outcomes were specified: • Policy framework guiding local service delivery established; • Local government councillors perceived as legitimate representatives; • Local governments have capacity to perform their designated functions; • Local governments effectively performing their service delivery functions. For objective two (Local governments are accountable and transparent) there were two outcomes to be assessed: • Community members (at district and village levels) able to hold their leaders and officials accountable; • Community members are actively engaged in the planning and management of service delivery.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative: i) District Development Frameworks (DDF). One of the most significant achievements of the programme is the way in which the Local Governments (LG) are now engaged in consultative processes with their communities in order to identify development needs and to prioritize possible interventions. The resulting DDF is an important tool for drawing up the Local Governments' annual work plans and budgets. The Outcome Evaluation of JPLG revealed that DDFs are now being used by NGOs and other agencies and this avoids wasteful duplication of efforts. There is however a serious imbalance in the manner in which DDFs are formulated. The emphasis is more about what the communities say they want rather than what sector professionals determine is technically feasible- or rational from a wider planning perspective. In addition, the links with national development plans or with the plans of line ministries are still very weak. ii) Civic EducationThe Outcome Evaluation pointed out that the civic education programmes being implemented in Puntland and Somaliland were infrequent, not reaching out to rural areas, transmittal rather than participatory, message giving rather than issue raising. Following this finding,the civic education strategy was revised and resource pack produced with guidelines for facilitators, scenarios for triggering discussion on local governance (LG) issues, and a toolkit of methods for promoting dialogues and interactive techniques. It is also having an impact going by the number of people in the Focus Group Discussions that know about LG structures and functions that have changed their perception about LG service delivery, and are actually involved in the various planning and consultative forums set by the programme.
